paragraphs: R. Yitzḥak bar Avdimi. Eruvin (89a): Abaye said, 'Have you not heard what R. Yitzḥak bar Avdimi said?' Pesaḥim (54a). There were two, as Tosafot writes: one was Rav's teacher, as in chapter Kol HaBasar and chapter HaSefinah; and we find at the beginning of Yevamot and in HaNisrafin one who was Rava's teacher. Of the first we find in Kirah that he entered the bathhouse after Rabbi; of the second, at the end of chapter Tefillat HaShaḥar: R. Yitzḥak bar Avdimi said in the name of our teacher. Rashi explains: Rav. In chapter Ein Omedin (33b) Rashi explains nothing, nor in Berakhot (44, beginning of side b); but in chapter Af Al Pi (56a) Rashi explains: Rav. This is Rav's student, Rabbah's teacher. (In my opinion: Rava's.) In Tosafot to that Af Al Pi passage: 'R. Yitzḥak bar Avdimi said in the name of our teacher'—Rashi explains: Rav. This is difficult, etc.; therefore the reading is that 'our teacher' is Rabbi, and the R. Yitzḥak bar Avdimi here is the early one, Rabbi's student, Rav's teacher, who taught him udder and measures. End of quotation. In Menaḥot (93, end of side a), Rav Ḥisda and R. Yitzḥak bar Avdimi. Tosafot writes here and below (98a) that it appears he was Rav Ḥisda's colleague (R. Yitzḥak bar Avdimi and Rav Ḥisda: one said [one view] and one said [the other], Ḥelek 100a). He was Rava's teacher, for Rava said, 'Rav Yitzḥak bar Avdimi told me: It is derived by “hennah,”' at the beginning of Yevamot (3a), and in Sanhedrin (75b), and there (51a and 87b), Keritot (5a). In Ḥagigah (11b), Rava said, 'R. Yitzḥak bar Avdimi told me'; Tosafot there writes that there were two. Another [Yitzḥak bar Avdimi] lived in Rabbi's days, as we find in chapter Kirah (40b): Rav Yitzḥak bar Avdimi once entered the bathhouse after Rabbi (see above, R. Yitzḥak Ruba). He was Rav's teacher, for Bava Batra (87, end of side a) says, 'Is there a tanna who taught Rav measures?' They pointed to Rav Yitzḥak bar Avdimi. Rashbam reads 'whom Rav taught,' without the lamed—that is, Rav taught him measures. Rabbenu Tam brings proof from chapter Kol HaBasar (110a) that he was Rav's teacher, for it says, 'Is there a tanna who taught Rav udder?' They pointed to R. Yitzḥak bar Avdimi. (Tosafot there writes: Yet it is possible that R. Yitzḥak bar Avdimi, Rav's teacher, lived until Rava, for on the day Rav Yehudah, Rav's student, died, Rava was born; and Rabbenu Tam said that there were two, etc.) One cannot read there 'whom Rav taught,' because he answers him, 'I taught him the udder of a nursing animal.' Some explain that 'to him' means 'from him,' as we find in Mo'ed Katan, 'If the many need him.' End of quotation. In Bava Batra (there): when R. Elazar went up, he found Ze'iri and said, 'Is there a tanna who taught Rav measures?' etc. Tosafot writes: Rabbenu Tam said there were two R. Yitzḥak bar Avdimis: one in Rabbi's days, in Kirah (there), who was Rav's teacher, and one in Rava's days, etc. However, רשב״א [provisionally R. Shimshon ben Avraham] said that the R. Yitzḥak bar Avdimi here must have been Rav's student. If you suppose he was Rav's teacher, how could he say to R. Elazar, 'But it was stated about this: R. Abbahu said: R. Yoḥanan said'? (Our present reading does not have 'R. Yoḥanan said.') For even R. Yoḥanan, R. Abbahu's teacher, called Rav—who was R. Yitzḥak bar Avdimi's student—'our teacher,' as we say in chapter Ellu Terefot (54). End of quotation. In Ḥullin (95b), R. Yoḥanan wrote to Rav, 'Before our teacher'; so too Tosafot to that Kol HaBasar passage writes. Thus, if Rav was R. Yoḥanan's teacher, all the more would Rav Yitzḥak bar Avdimi be R. Yoḥanan's teacher, and certainly R. Abbahu's teacher, since R. Abbahu was R. Yoḥanan's student, and R. Yoḥanan Rav's student. How, then, could R. Yitzḥak bar Avdimi say, 'But it was stated about this: R. Abbahu said: R. Yoḥanan said'? So too in Tosafot, Bava Metzia (40a), on 'And so Rabbah said,' they write that the reading is Rav, for Rabbah was Rav Ḥisda's student: how could Rav Ḥisda speak in his student's name? Tosafot likewise wonders in Ḥullin (14a) how Rav Huna brought proof from what Rav Ḥiyya bar Rav, who was junior to him, expounded. Consult the rules and you will find the opposite of Tosafot's words. It is surprising that Tosafot did not write thus at the aforementioned end of chapter Tefillat HaShaḥar, where Rashi explains 'in the name of our teacher' as Rav; they should have written their aforementioned argument. More surprising: in chapter HaḤoletz (45a) and at the end of chapter 7, R. Yitzḥak bar Avdimi said in the name of our teacher, and Rashi explains: Rabbi. Rava said: 'Any verse that R. Yitzḥak bar Avdimi has not explained remains unexplained,' Zevaḥim (43b); there (28, end of side a): 'Rather, Abaye said: When R. Yitzḥak bar Avdimi came' ('Rava said'—so it is in שס״ח [provisionally the new Shas]; in my opinion it should read 'Rabbah said'), 'rely on that which he taught,' etc.
